item.title: Dortmund "definitely" want to recruit a central defender in winter
item.description: Dortmund "definitely" want to recruit a central defender in winter Having made a strong start to the Bundesliga season, Borussia Dortmund may be set to bolster their squad depth in winter. As BVB chief journalist Jörg Weiler reports in the BILD podcast 'Dortmund Insider', the central defender position is to be improved. “From what I've heard, they definitely want to bring in another central defender, possibly even from the second division,” Weiler hinted. Weiler didn't list any names, but the fact is, however, that Dortmund has financial leeway in the winter transfer window. A talented defender like Hertha BSC's Linus Gechter (22) could be an option, who was linked with BVB back in October 2025. The bosses of the Westphalian outfit haven't set a fixed budget on their spending, but there is an internal agreement for recruitment. "If someone finds a player that everyone in charge [at Dortmund] is convinced of and can help BVB in the short term (…). "Then they [BVB are] certainly willing to open the coffers in the winter," says Weiler's colleague Maximilian Wessing.

item.title: Bernardo Silva opens up about his situation at Real Madrid – “I want to be useful”
item.description: Bernardo Silva opens up about his situation at Real Madrid – “I want to be useful” This international break will see Bernardo Silva taking on an elevated role for the Portuguese national team. Following Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, Silva has been appointed as the captain of the pack and he will play a key role in steering the team forward in the coming years. Speaking ahead of Portugal’s UEFA Nations League encounter against Denmark, Silva offered his perspective on his story so far at Real Madrid. Silva wants to feel useful Silva has adopted a deeper midfield role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) It is no secret that Silva has had a relatively slow start to life at Real Madrid, notably struggling for game-time in the initial phases. The former Man City star acknowledged that the Real Madrid team is stacked right now, but added he wants to feel useful in the team and that not playing enough always hurts. “It’s always difficult. We all want to play, we all want to be useful. In my career, I have always been used to being useful, to participating. When I don’t participate, it’s obviously tough. “The coach has 27 players, which are many, and only 11 can play at a time. It’s a pretty difficult job, to choose between such a talented team,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). Silva has made only seven starts in La Liga for Real Madrid this season, though he has been more prominent in Jose Mourinho’s plans in recent weeks. “What I can guarantee from me is that I will always give my best and I will always be willing to try to improve and help the team in whatever is necessary, whether it is 5, 10, 30 or 90 minutes. Of course, I want to participate and feel useful,” he added. Silva on playing further back Silva is now the capain of the Portugal team. (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images) Silva made his name in the game by being an illustrious playmaker who can offer creative spark going forward. At Real Madrid, he has adopted a deeper role, often appearing as the deep-lying playmaker. Talking about his position, Silva said, “Now I don’t know exactly why, but I’m more conservative, more thoughtful, very different than I was 10 years ago. That has led me to other positions, a little further back in the midfield. “But I am always available to try to help the National Team and my club in what the coach deems necessary. The coach will have to answer that question. I think he sees me as an 8, a 10, a link between defense and attack. And not as much as an extreme,” he added. Finally, Silva added what coaches now expect from him, now that he is no longer the dynamic playmaker he once was. “ Therefore, that balance between defense and attack, which makes transitions, which helps with the pressure. The player who does a little bit of everything is what the coach expects of me, ” he concluded.

Francis, a product of the NFL Academy in London, and freshman offensive lineman Nikau Hepi, who came from the NFL Academy’s campus in Australia, are the first NFL Academy athletes to play for the Seminoles. item.title: UC Bearcats at Iowa State Cyclones live updates, score, highlights
item.description: AMES, IA – It's brunch with the Bearcats as the University of Cincinnati kicks off at Jack Trice Stadium at 11 a.m. locally, noon in Cincinnati. Post bacon-and-eggs, UC hopes to pancake some Iowa State defenders at Jack Trice Stadium for that elusive sixth win and bowl eligibility. It would also be their first win in November since winning their first Big 12 game in Houston three years ago. They haven't won a road game since defeating Oklahoma State Oct. 18 of last season. After last week's one-score defeat at No. 17 Houston , UC is 1-12 in the 11th month of the year. The Bearcats are 5-4 (2-4 Big 12), with Iowa State's Cyclones coming in 4-5 (2-4 Big 12). Last season, UC defeated No. 14/No. 12 Iowa State at Nippert Stadium 38-30 in their best win of the season. The Cyclones have 83 new players, including Arkansas State transfer quarterback Jaylen Raynor, another dual-threat weapon. Former walk-on Aiden Flora has terrorized defenses with 1,119 rushing yards. Flora has been over 100 yards four times and had 212 yards in shootout wins vs. West Virginia and 221 vs. then-No. 24 Oklahoma State. Arizona, Utah, BYU and Iowa have been the only teams to keep Flora below the century mark. The Bearcats should have running back Cole Tabb back, who left the Houston game in the third quarter with a head injury . Tabb has 812 rushing yards and 14 total touchdowns to lead the Bearcats. UC should also have center Taran Tyo back on the offensive line, but will be without receiver JV Gibson, who left TDECU Stadium in Houston on a stretcher after sustaining a targeting hit in the end zone. item.title: Arsenal international provides fantastic assist in Ecuador win
item.description: Arsenal international provides fantastic assist in Ecuador win Piero Hincapie provided an assist in Ecuador’s win over Costa Rica overnight, as well as helping the team to keep a clean sheet. Photo by Franklin Jacome/Getty Images Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie made a start for Ecuador against Costa Rica on Friday night, or the early hours of Saturday morning in UK time. It was an impactful appearance, as the 24-year-old set up his team’s opening goal with a wonderful assist in the 22nd minute. Receiving the ball on the left-hand side near the halfway line, Hincapie spotted a gap in the opposition defence, and he slid a pass through to Jordy Caicedo . The striker rounded the goalkeeper and scored for 1-0. Photo by Franklin Jacome/Getty Images Hincapie almost repeated the same assist later in the half, with a very similar pass from a similar situation only narrowly failing to find the striker on that occasion. The defender then could have scored a goal of his own, early in the second half, forcing one of the saves of the match with a shot from the edge of the penalty area. At the other end, Hincapie did a good job of helping Ecuador to hold out until the 68th minute, at which point Costa Rica were reduced to 10 men and their hopes of a result began to fade. A Moises Caicedo penalty made sure of the 2-0 win in the latter stages, with Hincapie coming off shortly after that in the 85th minute. Hincapie has had some injury difficulties this season, only starting three matches for Arsenal in all competitions even when he’s been fit. So the Gunners will be glad to see him getting 85 minutes and playing well. Ecuador are in action once more before the international break ends, facing Bolivia on Tuesday night. Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images

item.title: Thieves Towed a £350,000 BTCC Audi From ExCeL London, Then FaceTimed Its Team Boss Asking for Cash
item.description: Adam Weaver, team principal of British Touring Car Championship outfit Power Maxed Racing, took a FaceTime call on Thursday night in which someone showed him the team's stolen Audi and asked him to bring cash to get it back. The car, driven by Dexter Patterson, is valued by the team at about £350,000. Weaver described the call to BBC Hereford & Worcester on Friday. He told the caller it was not happening that night, and the caller said he would be in touch in the morning. A second call, Weaver said, told him police had been alerted and the car was on a road still in London. Before the caller rang again, police told Weaver the car had been recovered close to ExCeL London. The Metropolitan Police told the BBC it does not comment on individual car thefts, so the recovery rests on the team's account. No arrests have been reported. Crews working on racing cars in a pit garage. Representative image, not Power Maxed Racing's team. Photo: Scott Foltz / Pexels How the trailer left the compound The team had brought the car to ExCeL for filming and promotional work. It was loaded into a trailer and left in the venue's secure car park overnight, wheel-clamped and backed up against another vehicle so the doors could not be opened, Weaver said. At about 02:30 GMT on Thursday, he was told, three people got into the site, brought in a vehicle and towed the trailer away with the car still inside. ExCeL London said on Thursday evening that it was aware of "an incident in relation to a vehicle theft" and that its security team was working with relevant stakeholders. The statement as reported does not say how the site was entered or how a clamped trailer was moved. Who would pay for it Dr Anthony Gunter, a criminologist at The Open University, told the BBC he believes the thieves wanted the trailer, which can be broken up and sold in parts, and had not realised the car was inside. His view is that a BTCC car has no market because everyone knows what it is. On that reading, the only person who would pay for it was the team. Social media is what Weaver credits for the outcome. Power Maxed's Facebook post thanked everyone who shared the earlier appeal and "made the car and trailer too hot to be handled." We covered the same pressure play in a stolen $500,000 McLaren in Detroit , where the owner asked 1.1 million followers to find it. The car and the team The team's own paperwork is not consistent on the car. Its announcement of Patterson, a 22-year-old Scot, for 2026 refers to a new Audi S3, while the BTCC's team listing gives the car as an Audi A3 Saloon. The BBC's reporting says only "Audi." The listing also puts the team's base at Weston Subedge near Evesham, while the BBC places it in Studley, Warwickshire. The BBC notes the team's former headquarters near Evesham was destroyed in a fire in 2025. BTCC cars are a regular sight at circuits such as Brands Hatch . item.title: What the numbers say about a winner in Cowboys vs 49ers
item.description: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards, two touchdowns and finished with a passer rating of 114.2 . He finished the game with a four-play, 65-yard game winning touchdown drive in just 29 seconds. CeeDee Lamb led the team with another massive performance through the air. He racked up an astonishing 195 receiving yards and one touchdown, also fumbling once on an odd play. Javonte Williams and Tyler Goodson finished with a combined 32 carries and 178 yards on the ground. item.title: Tyrrell Hatton comments on the state of his golf game after taking the solo lead on day three in Dubai
item.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images Tyrrell Hatton will head into the final round of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai on Sunday with a one-stroke lead. Hatton posted a third-round 68 to move one shot clear of Frenchman Victor Perez with 18 holes left to play. The Englishman is in fine form right now, following his runner-up finish in Abu Dhabi last week. Now Tyrrell Hatton will be hoping to close out his 2026 season in style with a win in Dubai on Sunday. Hatton cannot win the Race to Dubai title, but he would dearly love to win the DP World Tour Championship for the first time in his career. However, with Perez just one stroke behind him, and Rory McIlroy and Jon Rahm positioned well for a final-day charge, Hatton’s task on Sunday will be far from simple. Tyrrell Hatton comments on his golf game after taking the solo lead in Dubai The 35-year-old Englishman addressed the media after firing a third-round 68 on Saturday in Dubai, and he was asked to share how he feels about his golf game. “ Yeah, it was a good day. It was tricky, “ Hatton replied. “ The greens were so fast on the back nine. Every putt I had coming in I think from 13, the par 3, just unbelievably fast. Really happy with how I putted today. Had a few like awkward-length par putts early on, and managed to hold them, which was nice. “ Yeah, overall, just happy with how I played. Generally, I think my iron play has been pretty good these last two weeks. Last week I was really happy with my wedges. This week, it’s a little bit harder to get the wedges right to be honest. “ And then the other thing would be just the putter. I did a lot of work with the start line and reading putts and sort of visualising the ball going in. I think that’s shown these two weeks. “ But does Hatton fancy his chances of winning on Sunday in Dubai? “ I know tomorrow is going to be a tough day, “ the Englishman admitted. “ I’ve got enough experience down these last few holes to know that anything can happen. So yeah, I’ll just go out tomorrow and try my best. I know I can play well around here, and that’s what I’ll try to do. “

item.title: How much relief will the Spencers provide?
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 30: Atlanta Braves pitcher Spencer Strider (l), Braves pitcher Max Fried (54), Braves pitcher Charlie Morton (50) and Braves pitcher Spencer Schwellenbach (r) celebrate in the locker room after the Braves win the final regular season MLB baseball game of 2024 between the New York Mets and the Atlanta Braves on September 30, 2024 at Truist Park in Atlanta, Georgia. The Braves will go on to San Diego to play the Padres in the Wildcard playoff. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I was one of those fans surprised (yet not surprised) with the Evan Phillips signing. I can squint and see it working out, but it was probably one year and/or $2 MM AAV too much. With one reliever signed, the focus shifts to whether or not Raisel Iglesias returns. There is probably a number there that would make me comfortable with that. But another thought brings me to two pitchers that are recovering from injuries. Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach could serve anywhere from starters to swingmen to multiple inning guys to high leverage. That is, assuming they can pitch at all in 2027. Having trouble viewing this? Open in a new window . Alex Anthopoulos has already told us that he’s not counting on either to start the year in the rotation. But there is a lot of room between being a starter out of Spring Training and pitching at all. Spencer Strider has a career 3.45/2.83/2.72 in the first time through the order. That will definitely play and will play up in a one to two inning outing. Schwellenbach’s numbers are a juicy 2.04/2.79/2.91, which honestly sounds like a lot of fun in high leverage. Of course, if these guys can’t start, the rotation options after Chris Sale are young Didier Fuentes, the Grant Holmes Experience, Bryce Elder, AJ Smith-Shawver, Joey Wentz, JR Ritchie, and Owen Murphy. This is assuming Tyler Mahle doesn’t return. So how many relief innings will the Braves get from Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach? Will the Braves put them in a position to pitch fewer than three innings at a time? Will injury force their hand? See, this is why I wasn’t super excited for the offseason this year. Too many questions and too much time.

item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 13: Serge Gnabry of FC Bayern München visits a training session of the NFL Team New England Patriots at Saebener Strasse training ground on November 13, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images When in Munich, why not spend some time with FC Bayern? It is not every day that one of the NFL’s young quarterbacks gets to hang out with some of the biggest names in German soccer. Maye is in Munich as the Patriots take part in the final International Game of the NFL calendar this year. And apparently, his trip has included a little time wi th local soccer royalty, too. Who knows? Maybe a few Bayern players will return the favor and show up at an NFL game sometime soon. The meeting was shared by @iMiaSanMia on X. Join the conversation! item.title: Como sets high asking price for Juventus target
item.description: Como sets high asking price for Juventus target Several players at Como have been performing impressively this season, helping Cesc Fabregas’ side exceed expectations. Their form has attracted interest from major clubs, but Como are determined to keep their most important players as they look to maintain their progress. One of the players attracting attention is Martin Baturina, who has emerged as a transfer target for Juventus. The Bianconeri are interested in bringing the attacking midfielder to Turin after watching him make a strong impression since joining Como. Baturina has been in excellent form and has established himself as an important member of Fabregas’ team. Juventus believe he has the qualities to make a difference in their squad, but securing his signature could prove difficult given his importance to Como. Juventus target Como midfielder The midfielder’s performances have helped Como establish themselves as one of the most impressive sides in the league. His contribution has made him an important player for the club, meaning they have little reason to allow him to leave without receiving a substantial fee. According to TuttoJuve , Como want around €80m for the midfielder, reflecting how highly they rate him and the importance they attach to keeping him in their squad. (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images) Como place huge valuation on Baturina An €80m asking price would make any potential move a major investment for Juventus. Although the Bianconeri are a much bigger club and could appeal to the 23-year-old, Como’s valuation means they would need to make a significant financial commitment. Baturina could be attracted by the opportunity to join Juventus and take the next step in his career. However, the size of the proposed fee could complicate negotiations, particularly if the Bianconeri are unwilling to spend that much on one player. Como will want to retain a key figure in their squad, while Juventus must decide whether Baturina is worth the asking price. For now, the midfielder’s future remains uncertain, with his performances continuing to attract attention.

(Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Playoff hopes are on life support for the Tigers, so if they don’t handle business on Saturday night in Death Valley, none of this will actually matter. item.title: Steve Smith Sr says he has one big question mark around Kirk Cousins after Vikings return
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Kirk Cousins feels like a much-needed new addition for the Minnesota Vikings but Steve Smith Sr still has one concern. Cousins has previously shone for the Vikings, managing over 4,000 passing yards in four of his previous seasons with the NFL outfit. That return should be especially helpful in 2026 as Minnesota’s current quarterback options have been pretty subpar. However, when speaking to ESPN this week, Smith has expressed concerns about Cousins’ arm strength. He also suggested that the Las Vegas Raiders’ willingness to trade him this season was in part due to his arm strength being an issue. Smith said: “My question mark is: what and how does Kevin O’Connell deal with the lack of arm strength that Kirk Cousins has this go-round? “Yes, because what he was before was a younger Kirk. But you can see, which I believe had something to do with the Las Vegas Raiders allowing him to go to Minnesota, that his lack of arm strength was an issue. “His arm, really. He had some underthrown throws, which led to him now being an opportunity for Minnesota, and it gave the Las Vegas Raiders an opportunity. Based on what I’m hearing, they feel like he’s ready.” Still, even if he is not the player he was back in 2023, he should still be an upgrade on Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz, who have managed fewer passing yards combined than Cousins in 2026. Cousins could make his second debut on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers and it will be interesting to see how much of an impact he has on the Vikings’ offence. Read more: Stephen A. The ‘Cats will struggle to get anything going offensively against a defense riddled with five-stars, and OSU freshman backup quarterback Luke Fahey won’t be asked to do any more than hand the ball off and lob it over the top to Jeremiah Smith. After getting shut out in the first half of the ballgame, the ‘Cats finished with just 10 points. Its receivers couldn’t get separation on Iowa’s defensive backs and Marchiol was under duress all day long, forced to scramble 23 times. Fortunately, though Northwestern will be without starting quarterback Aidan Chiles for a second-straight weekend, the ‘Cats’ offensive outlook should improve in Columbus. Iowa has the best defense in the Big Ten, and though Ohio State’s is also good, it has been vulnerable in recent weeks. The Buckeyes have given up over 30 points in back-to-back weeks, in losses to USC and Oregon. So, I do think Northwestern will score a few more points than last week. But the bad news is that I don’t think it’ll have any defensive answer for Jeremiah Smith and Ohio State’s offense. With injuries still haunting NU’s secondary, expect Smith to finish will over 100 yards and a couple touchdowns in route to a double-digit Ohio State victory.

The match was played in front of a noticeably sparse crowd at La Bombonera, marking a stark contrast to the usual atmosphere surrounding the world champions. Scaloni avoids attendance controversy The atmosphere at La Bombonera on Wednesday night was unusually quiet as Argentina faced Uruguay . Following the retirement of Messi, the national team appeared to lose some of its box-office appeal, with thousands of seats remaining empty for the clash. Scaloni, who recently committed his future to the team until 2030, was quick to downplay the significance of the low turnout during his post-match media duties. "I don't know how many people were there, I didn't even think about it. I don't have an opinion on that. I don't know what to tell you," Scaloni stated when questioned about the lack of supporters, as quoted by La Nacion . Boss insists loyalty outlasts the Messi era Despite the sobering sight of empty stands at La Bombonera, Argentina's coaching staff remains adamant that the deep-rooted bond between the national team and its supporters is unbreakable. While the sparse attendance in one of Buenos Aires' most iconic footballing strongholds hinted at the reality of a looming transitional era, the manager dismissed any suggestion that fan loyalty hinges solely on the presence of their talismanic number 10, Messi. item.title: De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain
item.description: Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid From the London Palladium to Madrid’s Metropolitano, they’re all here. On Sunday night, the footballers who lifted the game’s biggest awards meet again three weeks later and on the field this time, dinner jackets but not a single man left behind. Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or and Gerd Müller trophy winner. Unai Simón, holder of the Lev Yashin award . Luis de la Fuente , the coach of the year who on Thursday night announced that also joining them will be Lamine Yamal , the kid who lifted the Kopa award as the best young player for the third year running and said he would have preferred Pau Cubarsí to be standing there instead. And, yes, Cubarsí will be there too for the final Nations League group game. At 1.45pm the world and European champions landed back at Madrid’s Barajas airport from Prague, where they had won again, before making their way by bus to their Las Rozas HQ, around the M40 motorway to the north-west of the capital. At about the same time, Lamine Yamal arrived from Barcelona, due in at midday. As was Mikel Oyarzabal , scorer of the winner at Euro 2024 and Spain’s top marksman this summer (not that he would ever tell you so) from San Sebastián. At 7.30pm, they trained, preparing to meet the World Cup semi-finalists and the team they defeated in Berlin at the end of Euro 2024. Two starters from the World Cup final will be absent: Dani Olmo and the captain, 2024 Ballon d’Or winner Rodri , are injured. But everyone else will be there. Continue reading...

item.title: Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?
item.description: The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play their first game without him . The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7. The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. item.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
item.description: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player . You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
